sources.entry: mbeaudru/modern-js-cheatsheet: cheatsheet for the JavaScript knowledge you will frequently encounter in modern projects.

summary.one_liner: A long-form cheatsheet explaining modern (ES2015+) JavaScript features such as let/const, arrow functions, destructuring, promises, and classes for developers who find contemporary codebases hard to read.
summary.what_it_does: The guide is organized as a table of contents followed by one section per language feature. Each section gives a short explanation, sample code with inline comments showing expected output, and a list of external resources. Covered topics include variable declarations (var, let, const) with scope and temporal dead zone, arrow functions and the lexical this, default parameters, destructuring, spread and rest, object property shorthand, map/filter/reduce/find, promises, template literals and tagged templates, ES modules import/export, this binding, classes, extends and super, async/await, truthy/falsy values, generators, and static methods. It is explicitly not a tutorial from scratch and is aimed at readers who know basic JavaScript. The README also contains a glossary section listing scope and variable mutation.
use_cases: learning ES6 syntax before reading React code
looking up how let, const and var differ
understanding arrow functions and this binding
refreshing array map, filter, reduce and find
understanding ES module import and export
notable: Focuses on the syntax you meet in modern projects and sample code, not on teaching JavaScript from scratch
Each section pairs short explanations with sample code showing outputs in comments
Personal recommendations are flagged as such, for example always using const by default
Curated external resources (MDN, WesBos, Yehuda Katz and others) listed per topic
caveats: Assumes basic JavaScript knowledge; it is not a beginner course
Some sections are a bit dated relative to newer language features, since it centers on ES2015/ES6
Some examples use jQuery ($.get) and older patterns for comparison
